claims.source_quote_ar: أَفَأَمِنُوا مَكْرَ اللَّهِ فَلا يَأْمَنُ مَكْرَ اللَّهِ إِلا الْقَوْمُ الْخَاسِرُونَ
claims.claim_ar: تكرار عبارة «مَكْرَ اللَّهِ» في الآية لتوكيد المعنى والتنبيه إلى خطورة المكر الإلهي وعدم أمْنِه لمن ظن أنه آمن.
claims.claim_en: Repetition of the phrase 'مَكْرَ اللَّهِ' to emphasize and warn about the danger of God's plotting and that it is not to be trusted by those who presume security.

claims.source_quote_ar: أَفَأَمِنُوا مَكْرَ اللَّهِ فَلا يَأْمَنُ مَكْرَ اللَّهِ
claims.claim_ar: مقابلة وبناء توازٍ بين تصور الناس بأمنهم من مكر الله وبين الحقيقة بأن مكر الله لا يُؤمَن، أيّ تركيب تبايني يكشف المفارقة ويوضح الجزع والعاقبة.
claims.claim_en: A parallel/antithetical structure contrasting people's assumed safety from God's plotting with the reality that God's plotting cannot be felt secure against; a balancing structure that reveals the paradox and the resulting doom.
claims.needs_review_reason: Classification as muqabalah (balanced antithesis) could alternatively be described as tibaq or general antithesis; rhetorical label may vary by tradition.

claims.source_quote_ar: فَلا يَأْمَنُ مَكْرَ اللَّهِ إِلا الْقَوْمُ الْخَاسِرُونَ
claims.claim_ar: استعمال أداة الاستثناء «إِلَّا» لحصر النتيجة بمن هم الخاسرون، فتؤكّد استثناءًا صارمًا ودلالة تأديبية على جزاء الكفر والإصرار.
claims.claim_en: Use of the exception particle 'إِلَّا' to confine the outcome to 'the losing people', emphasizing a strict exclusion and disciplinary consequence for disbelief and persistence.
claims.needs_review_reason: «إلا» is a grammatical particle; its labeling as a rhetorical device (hasr/qasr) is interpretive and may be treated as grammar rather than stylistic device in some frameworks.

claims.claim_ar: استعمال لفظ «مَكْر» مع الله في موضع يدلّ على معانٍ مَعْنَوِيّة (مثل الاستدراج والانتقام الإلهي)؛ قراءة تفسيرية قد تُعامل كاستعمال مجازي أو كناية عن ترويض العاصين.
claims.claim_en: Use of the word 'مَكْر' applied to God indicating non-literal meanings (such as 'luring/gradual punishment' or divine retribution); a interpretive usage that can be treated as metaphorical or figurative (majaz/kinaya).
claims.needs_review_reason: Whether this is classified as majaz (metaphor) or literal/theological language depends on exegesis; Tabari treats it as 'استدراج' (practical/operational meaning) rather than a simple figure of speech.

warnings: Source-chunks provided are from Zamakhshari and Tabari; the user requested extraction from al-Jurjani, al-Sakkaki, al-Baqillani, al-Suyuti and tafsir-balagha materials. Those specified authors' chunks were not provided, so claims are drawn from the available Tabari chunk (and other supplied chunks where relevant).

Some classifications (e.g., labeling «إِلَّا» as hasr_qasr or reading «مَكْرَ اللَّهِ» as majaz) are interpretive and may vary across rhetorical/tafsir traditions; check with the preferred authorial framework if strict mapping is required.
